Bash(gh issue close 26 --comment "$\(cat <<''EOF''
## Resolution

Button mapping confirmed working correctly with original GPIO assignments:

| Physical Button | GPIO | Function |
|-----------------|------|----------|
| A \(leftmost\) | 9 | Navigate backwards |
| B \(middle\) | 6 | Navigate forwards |
| C \(rightmost\) | 5 | Reserved |

The initial report of "reversed" buttons was due to confusion about expected behavior, not incorrect GPIO mapping.

**Note:** ESP32-S3 Feather uses the same OLED FeatherWing button mapping as M0/M4/nRF52840 boards \(GPIO 9, 6, 5\), NOT the standard ESP32 mapping \(GPIO 15, 32, 14\). Using standard ESP32 pins causes boot loop since GPIO 32 doesn''t exist on ESP32-S3.

## Testing
- ✅ Button A navigates backwards
- ✅ Button B navigates forwards
- ✅ Button C no action \(reserved\)
- ✅ No reboot loops
EOF
\)")

Bash(gh issue create --title "Integrate SHT41 for accurate temperature/humidity" --body "$\(cat <<''EOF''
## Summary
Add Sensirion SHT41 sensor for accurate temperature and humidity readings, separate from BME688.

## Motivation
- BME688 has self-heating from gas heater causing ~5°F temperature offset
- BSEC2 library proving complex to configure properly
- SHT41 provides ±0.2°C accuracy without self-heating issues

## Hardware
- **Sensor:** Adafruit SHT41 \(PID 5776\)
- **Interface:** I2C \(0x44\)
- **Connection:** STEMMA QT daisy-chain

## Implementation Tasks
- [ ] Install Adafruit SHT4x library
- [ ] Add SHT41 initialization
- [ ] Read temp/humidity from SHT41 instead of BME688
- [ ] Update Environment screen to show SHT41 temp/humidity
- [ ] Keep BME688 for gas/pressure/IAQ only
- [ ] Update OLED compact view
- [ ] Consider external/vented mounting for best accuracy

## Sensor Comparison
| Spec | SHT41 | SHT45 | BME688 |
|------|-------|-------|--------|
| Temp accuracy | ±0.2°C | ±0.1°C | ±1.0°C + self-heat |
| RH accuracy | ±1.8% | ±1.0% | ±3% |

## Notes
- SHT45 is drop-in compatible if it comes back in stock
- Same library, same I2C address, same code

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] SHT41 detected on I2C scan at 0x44
- [ ] Temperature within ±1°F of reference thermometer
- [ ] Humidity readings stable and reasonable
EOF
\)" --label "type:enhancement")

Bash(gh issue create --title "Make TFT sleep timeout configurable \(0 = disabled\)" --body "$\(cat <<''EOF''
## Summary
Allow TFT sleep timeout to be configured, including disabled entirely \(0 = always on\).

## Motivation
- LCDs don''t suffer from burn-in like OLEDs
- User may want TFT as a permanent status display running 24/7
- Power consumption is acceptable for always-on use cases

## Implementation
- Change `TFT_SLEEP_TIMEOUT` to support 0 as "disabled"
- Update `checkDisplaySleep\(\)` to skip TFT sleep when timeout is 0
- Default to 0 \(disabled\) since LCD burn-in is not a concern

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] TFT_SLEEP_TIMEOUT = 0 keeps TFT always on
- [ ] TFT_SLEEP_TIMEOUT > 0 enables sleep after specified duration
- [ ] OLED sleep behavior unchanged \(still has timeout for burn-in protection\)
EOF
\)" --label "type:enhancement")

Bash(gh issue create --title "GPS screen display corruption when acquiring fix" --body "$\(cat <<''EOF''
## Bug Description
GPS screen shows display corruption when transitioning between "Acquiring fix" state and valid fix state. Screen doesn''t repaint properly - yellow "Acquiring fix" text visible behind green coordinate numbers.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Start device without GPS fix
2. Wait for GPS to acquire fix
3. Observe display artifacts on GPS screen

## Expected Behavior
Screen should fully repaint when GPS state changes from acquiring to valid fix.

## Likely Cause
Screen update logic doesn''t clear the full display area when GPS validity state changes.

## Suggested Fix
Add `tft.fillScreen\(COLOR_BG\)` or targeted `fillRect\(\)` when `gpsData.valid` transitions from false to true.
EOF
\)" --label "type:bug")

- A3 = GPIO 15 \(was 14\)
- A4 = GPIO 14 \(was 8\)
